title: 2 Assessing the effects of parasitism and long-term freezing on quality of goat meat using Bioelectrical Impedance Analysis
content:
Abstract
Meat quality is influenced by numerous factors, including the health status of the animals and length of storage in a freezer. Assessing these factors efficiently can help improve meat production, quality, and safety. In this study, a total of sixteen intact male Spanish goats (8 healthy and 8 naturally infected with internal parasites) were used to collect carcass loin chops for evaluating the differences in resistance (Rs) and reactance (Xc) values using Bioelectrical Impedance Analysis (BIA). BIA is a non-invasive technique that sends a low electrical current through tissues and measures how the current passes through them, providing insights into tissue composition and health status. This study compared Rs and Xc between parasitized and healthy goats’ loin chops to evaluate meat quality, as well as assessed the differences in Rs and Xc values between fresh and long-term frozen (10 months) loin chops from healthy animals using BIA. The data were analyzed using GLIMMIX procedure in SAS. The results showed significantly higher (P < 0.05) Rs and Xc values in the loin chops from healthy goats (Rs = 545.7 ± 23.8; Xc = 109.1 ± 5.4) compared to those from parasitized goats (Rs = 430.3 ± 21.7; Xc = 93.9 ± 4.9). Additionally, Rs values were significantly higher (P < 0.05) in the long-term frozen loin chops (648.2 ± 16.5) compared to the fresh loin chops (195.3 ± 21.7), and the Xc values were significantly higher (P < 0.05) in the fresh loin chops (162.14 ± 5.0) compared to the frozen loin chops (65.5 ± 3.8), suggesting that long-term freezing affects the electrical characteristics of the meat, which may be due to changes in its moisture content, texture, or muscle composition. These findings suggest that BIA could be a useful tool for assessing meat quality, as it can detect differences in freshness, parasitism, and long-term freezing. This non-invasive method could help improve meat quality assessment, monitor animal health, and better understand the factors that influence the properties of meat.
